title: Where to Buy Ladies' Fashion Online in Pakistan
summary: Where to buy ladies' fashion online in Pakistan: six channels compared, sizing checks that work from a photo, and the COD and returns rules.
body_markdown:
Ladies' fashion sells online in Pakistan through six channels: brand websites, large marketplaces, Instagram and Facebook boutiques, unstitched fabric and lawn sellers, reseller and wholesale platforms, and cross-border apps that ship from China. Each prices differently, sizes differently and handles returns differently.


Pick the channel by what you are buying. A brand website is the safer route for a lawn suit or an occasion piece where fabric and finish have to be right. Marketplaces are fastest for everyday kurtis, shoes and bags. Social boutiques carry the newest trends and the least accountability. Reseller platforms exist for people buying stock to sell on. Cross-border apps carry the lowest stickers and the longest wait.


Below: what each channel is actually good at, the four checks that stop a bad order, how to get sizing right from a photo, and the reseller version of the same question.


## The six places to buy ladies' fashion online in Pakistan


These are six different trades that happen to sell overlapping catalogues. Most bad orders come from buying the wrong category in the wrong channel — a wedding outfit from an anonymous page, or a basic everyday kurti at full brand price.


### 1. Brand websites and official stores


Every established Pakistani clothing label runs its own online store, and that store is the only place where the stock is guaranteed to be the label's own. You get a published size chart, named fabric, a stated return policy and a customer service number that stays connected.


You pay retail for that. What retail buys you is predictability: the fabric is what the tag says, the colour matches the shoot within reason, and an exchange is a process rather than a favour.


**Best for:** lawn and formal collections, occasion wear, anything you need to be exactly as pictured.


### 2. Large marketplaces


Horizontal marketplaces carry the widest fashion catalogue and the most sellers per item. The same kurti design appears under a dozen store names at a dozen prices, and the listing photo is often lifted from the original brand's shoot rather than shot on that seller's actual stock.


That is the trap in clothing specifically. With a phone case, a copied photo costs you a small mismatch. With a garment, it costs you a different fabric weight, a different colour and a different cut. Read the **seller** reviews, not the product reviews, and look for buyer photos in the review section — those are the only images shot on the real item.


**Best for:** everyday stitched wear, shoes, bags and accessories where the downside is small.


### 3. Instagram and Facebook boutiques


Social selling carries an enormous share of Pakistani women's fashion, and much of it is honest. It is also where the least accountable stock lives: no listing history, no dispute system, no record of the order beyond a chat thread.


Rules that make this channel workable: insist on cash on delivery, ask for a video of the actual piece rather than the catalogue photo, ask for flat measurements in inches, and check whether the page leaves comments enabled. A page with comments switched off and only a highlights reel is telling you something.


**Best for:** trend-led pieces, small-batch stitched wear, sellers you have bought from before.


### 4. Unstitched fabric and lawn sellers


A large part of Pakistani women's clothing is still bought unstitched — three-piece lawn, cotton, khaddar in winter — and then tailored. Buying online here is a different exercise: you are judging fabric and print, not fit, and fit is settled later by your tailor.


Ask for the fabric weight or at least the composition, and ask for a photo of the cloth in daylight. Prints photograph brighter than they hang. If you are shopping the pieces that finish the outfit,[this roundup of Pakistani dupattas](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/best-pakistani-dupattas-for-women-in-pakistan) is a useful reference for what to look for in weave and drape.


**Best for:** lawn season, winter fabric, anyone with a tailor they trust.


### 5. Reseller and wholesale platforms


These are built for people buying stock rather than buying an outfit. Prices sit at a reseller tier instead of a retail tier, catalogues are organised by category rather than by label, and the platform handles delivery and cash collection. Markaz sits here — the[Markaz product categories](https://www.markaz.app/shop/categories) show how women's clothing, footwear, bags and jewellery are grouped, and you can look through the[supplier list](https://www.markaz.app/shop/supplier/list) to see who is actually behind the stock.


Ordinary shoppers can buy here too, and often do, because the price is below retail. The trade-off is that catalogues are organised for sellers: less styling, more specification. If you want the retail-versus-reseller comparison written out for fashion specifically,[Laam vs Markaz](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/laam-vs-markaz-pakistani-fashion-marketplace) puts a curated fashion marketplace next to a reseller catalogue on price, delivery and returns.


**Best for:** buying several pieces at once, and anyone buying to resell.


### 6. Cross-border apps shipping from China


Fast-fashion apps carry the lowest sticker prices and the deepest trend catalogue. The cost is time and uncertainty: long transit, sizing cut for a different market, customs handling that varies, and a return path that usually is not worth using from Pakistan.


Order one piece before you order five, and read the sizing in centimetres rather than trusting the S/M/L label.[Shein in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/shein-in-pakistan) covers delivery and customs on that route, and[the best Shein alternative in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/best-shein-alternative-in-pakistan) covers what to do when the wait or the sizing does not work. If you want the China catalogue with the import handled for you,[Markaz China categories](https://www.markaz.app/china/categories) land in about 10–17 days on cash on delivery.


**Best for:** trend testing, low-risk items, buyers who can wait.


## Match the channel to what you are buying


Category decides risk. These are the ones people ask about most.


- **Everyday stitched kurtis and co-ords.** Marketplaces and reseller platforms. Low downside, wide choice, and the price gap between channels is real.
- **Unstitched lawn and formal fabric.** Brand stores and specialist fabric sellers. You are buying cloth, so print accuracy and composition matter more than fit.
- **Wedding and occasion wear.** Brand stores, or a boutique with a physical address. This is the one category where paying more for accountability is the cheaper decision.
- **Abayas and modest wear.** Specialist sellers and reseller catalogues. Ask for length in inches from shoulder to hem — the single measurement that decides whether it works.
- **Shoes.** Marketplaces and reseller platforms, but only where a size chart in centimetres exists. Pakistani, UK and EU sizing are labelled interchangeably and are not the same.
- **Bags.** Anywhere, as long as the listing shows the inside. A bag photographed only from the front is hiding the lining and the stitching.
- **Artificial jewellery.** Reseller platforms and specialist pages. Plating quality is what separates a piece that lasts a season from one that marks the skin in a week;[this guide to artificial jewellery brands in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/best-artificial-jewellery-brands-in-pakistan) is a reasonable starting list.


## Sizing: where most online fashion orders go wrong


Pakistani ready-to-wear sizing is not standardised. One label's medium is another's small, and a cross-border app's medium is smaller than both. Ignore the letter and work in inches.


The method that works: take a garment you already own and like the fit of, lay it flat, and measure chest across the front, shoulder seam to shoulder seam, sleeve from shoulder seam to cuff, and full length from the highest point of the shoulder. Those four numbers are your size. Ask the seller for the same four for the piece you want.


Any seller who cannot give flat measurements for a stitched garment either has not seen the stock or does not want you to compare. Both are reasons to skip the order. For unstitched fabric the question is different — ask how many metres are in the shirt piece, and whether the trouser and dupatta lengths are cut for a tall frame.


## Four checks before you press order


- **Is the fabric named?** "Premium quality" is not a fabric. Lawn, cambric, khaddar, linen, viscose, chiffon, georgette — a seller who knows the stock names it, and the name tells you how it will wear in Karachi heat versus a Lahore winter.
- **Are there real photos?** A studio shoot plus at least one plain photo of the actual piece, ideally in daylight. Trend colours are the ones that photograph least accurately; mustard, teal and dusty pink all shift under artificial light.
- **Is the finish shown?** For stitched wear, ask for a close photo of the neckline and the sleeve hem. That is where cheap stitching shows first, and it is the part no catalogue photo frames.
- **What is the return window, in writing?** Before you order, not after. A platform with a published policy is a different proposition from a page that will "see what we can do".


## Cash on delivery, returns and what you are actually entitled to


COD is the default for online fashion in Pakistan and it is the main thing protecting a first-time buyer. But COD only protects you up to the doorstep — once you have paid the rider, you are inside whatever return policy the seller runs.


Two things to settle before ordering. First, whether the courier allows you to open the parcel before paying, because that varies by courier and by seller. Second, the return window and who pays return shipping. On Markaz, orders run on cash on delivery with a 7-day return window and orders inside Pakistan generally arrive in 3–5 days, so the terms are the platform's rather than an individual seller's mood.


Keep the packaging until you have tried the piece on. A return refused because the polybag was cut open is the most common way a valid claim dies.


## Red flags on a ladies' fashion listing


- **One photo, borrowed from a brand shoot.** Reverse-search it if the price looks unusual. If the image belongs to a label and the seller is not that label, you are buying a copy of unknown quality.
- **No measurements anywhere.** Covered above, and it is the strongest single signal.
- **"Colour may vary slightly" doing heavy lifting.** Reasonable for a shade. Not reasonable when the actual piece arrives in a different colour family.
- **Advance payment demanded for a first order.** On a channel where COD is normal, insisting on transfer is a choice the seller is making for a reason.
- **Comments and reviews disabled.** On social pages, this removes the only public record of how previous orders went.


## Buying ladies' fashion to resell, not to wear


If you are buying stock rather than an outfit, the question changes. You need a price you can mark up, stock you do not have to buy in bulk, and a delivery promise you can repeat to a customer.


Retail channels do not work for this. A brand store sells at the price your customer could pay directly, and a marketplace listing is visible to that customer too. What works is a reseller-tier catalogue: order at supplier pricing, list at your own price, and let the platform deliver and collect the cash. That is the model the[Markaz reseller programme](https://www.markaz.app/reseller-pk) runs on — no minimum order quantity, so you can list a design first and order the single unit once someone actually buys it.


Fashion has one complication that accessories do not: the size and colour matrix. Ten designs in four sizes and three colours is 120 things to track. New resellers do better starting with free-size or single-size items — abayas, dupattas, bags, jewellery, shawls — and adding sized clothing once the selling side works. That is also why many resellers start in an adjacent category first; the same channel logic applies to[where to buy mobile accessories online in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/where-to-buy-mobile-accessories-online-in-pakistan) , where there is no size matrix at all.


Three guides worth reading before you order stock:[selling wholesale clothing online in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/wholesale-clothing) for how the supply side is priced,[how to start a clothing store online in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/clothing-store-online) for the setup, and[how to reduce COD returns](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/reduce-cod-returns-pakistan) — because in clothing, returns are the number that decides whether the margin survives.


## A simple routine that works


Write down the four measurements from a garment that fits you. Decide which category you are buying and pick the matching channel from the list above. Ask for flat measurements and one daylight photo. Confirm the return window in writing. Order one piece from a seller before you order several.


That routine takes a few minutes and removes most of what goes wrong with buying clothes from a photograph.


## Frequently asked questions


### Where is the cheapest place to buy ladies' fashion online in Pakistan?


On sticker price, cross-border apps shipping from China. On price you can use this week, reseller and wholesale platforms, because they sit below the retail markup while still delivering locally. Marketplaces fall in between and vary seller by seller.


### Is it safe to buy clothes online with cash on delivery?


COD is the safest common option, because you are not paying for something that never arrives. It does not protect you from a piece that arrives in the wrong size or fabric, which is what the measurement and return-policy checks above are for.


### How do I know a stitched kurti will fit before I order?


Do not trust S/M/L. Measure a garment you already own flat — chest, shoulder, sleeve and full length — and ask the seller for the same four numbers in inches. If they cannot supply them, order elsewhere.


### How long does delivery take for clothing bought online in Pakistan?


Stock already in the country usually arrives within a few days; Markaz local orders run 3–5 days. Anything shipping from China takes much longer — Markaz China orders land in about 10–17 days, and unmanaged cross-border parcels can take longer still.


### Can I buy ladies' fashion online to resell without buying in bulk?


Yes, on a no-minimum platform. Markaz has no minimum order quantity, so you can list a design and order one unit when a customer buys it, instead of putting money into stock that may not move. Start with free-size categories before you take on a full size matrix.


### What should I check first on a listing?


The fabric name and the measurements. Those two decide whether the piece is what you think it is. Everything else — brand, styling, discount badge — is decoration around them.
